reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight lies in the interplay between orientation rules and Markov equivalence classes in causal discovery. R5, R6, and R7 operate on cycles and uncovered paths to enforce structural constraints ensuring that the resulting graph remains Markov equivalent to the true causal structure. These rules prevent incorrect orientations that would introduce spurious colliders or violate ancestral properties. The use of potentially directed paths (p.d.) allows for systematic traversal of causal relationships while respecting latent variable structures. Joined Graphs offer a syntactic simplification by abstracting away distinctions between tails and circles, yet they lose information critical for identifying real versus pseudo tails. This duality necessitates careful application of orientation rules to maintain validity across different graph representations. The failure mode occurs when selection bias is present but ignored, leading to incorrect edge orientations and thus invalid causal conclusions.
